html:
SMTO-FIL-0031 — This Windows file name or path isn't supported

GUID: 84f32175-14f1-46eb-b97a-b656b9602915
Slug: file-unsupported-path-feature
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use this path because part of it means something special to Windows, such as a reserved name like CON or NUL, a name ending in a dot or space, or an extra colon. SMTO didn't open or change it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look for a folder or file named CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9 or LPT1 to LPT9, even with an extension like nul.txt, and use a different name. Windows reserves these names for devices, so SMTO won't treat them as files.
  2. Remove any dot or space at the end of a folder or file name, and any colon except the one right after the drive letter. Trailing dots, trailing spaces and extra colons can make Windows open a different file than the one you meant.
  3. Write the full path with a backslash after the drive letter, like C:\Projects\report.txt, not C:Projects or a path starting with \?\ or \.. SMTO only accepts ordinary paths, not drive-relative or special device paths.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the file or folder and shows its result in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't keep sending the same path; it will be refused the same way until the name or path is changed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway File operation rejected a Windows path before any filesystem access because it contains an alternate-data-stream colon, a \.\ or \?\ device prefix, a drive-relative form (C:foo), a reserved DOS device name, or a component ending in a dot or space.

What this means

  • Windows path validation rejects alternate streams/device prefixes, drive-relative forms, reserved DOS names or components ending with a dot/space. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Windows path validation rejects alternate streams/device prefixes, drive-relative forms, reserved DOS names or components ending with a dot/space.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect target-native components and drive syntax rather than changing a valid source filename blindly.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the requested path in the receipt (rejected by file_common.validate_path) and rewrite it as a drive-rooted path (C:\dir\file) or a plain relative path with ordinary components; rename files or folders that use reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-COM9, LPT1-LPT9) or trailing dots/spaces with native Windows tools. These forms are intentionally unsupported and cannot be enabled.
  • Remove unsupported or reserved path components and use supported platform syntax.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen Windows path uses supported ordinary components.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
